title: Spontaneous magnetic diode effect in Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$
authors: Yining Hu, Taikang Chen, Jan Priessnitz, Zili Feng, Takashi Kurumaji, Linda Ye, Libor Šmejkal, Chunyu Mark Guo, Philip J. W. Moll
abstract: When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.
summary: This work reports the observation of a spontaneous magnetic diode effect in $	ext{Co}_{1/3}	ext{TaS}_2$, a phenomenon where current flow asymmetry is dictated by the internal magnetic order. The effect is theoretically attributed to the coupling between noncoplanar spin textures and spin-orbit coupling, distinguishing it from field-dependent magnetochiral effects. This provides a new platform for magnetically controlled, non-reciprocal electronic transport.
main_problem: The paper demonstrates a spontaneous magnetic diode effect (SMD) in $	ext{Co}_{1/3}	ext{TaS}_2$, where the diode's directionality is set by internal magnetism rather than crystal structure.
main_result: A pronounced, switchable non-reciprocal resistance (SMD) was observed, originating from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, even when the net magnetization vanishes.
method: The study combines experimental measurements of second-harmonic voltage ($V_{2\omega}$) with theoretical calculations using a tight-binding model incorporating spin-orbit coupling.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Co}_{1/3}	ext{TaS}_2$, a magnetic intercalation compound with a triangular lattice structure exhibiting non-coplanar magnetic order. The theory models this using a spin Hamiltonian and a tight-binding model on the lattice.
key_observables: Second-harmonic voltage ($V_{2\omega}$), anomalous Hall voltage ($V_H$), scalar spin chirality ($\chi_{	ext{local}}$), and the nonlinear Drude conductivity ($\sigma_{	ext{NLDrude}}$).
important_parameters: The effect is linked to the low-temperature chiral magnetic order, vanishing at $T_{N2} \approx 26.5 	ext{ K}$.
main_assumptions: The micro-machining process preserves the intrinsic magnetism, and the analysis relies on separating the non-reciprocal $V_{2\omega}$ signal from other time-reversal odd effects like the Hall voltage.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the symmetry breaking required for the effect, show $V_{2\omega}$ hysteresis loops whose sign reverses with spin reversal, and present theoretical calculations of the nonlinear conductivity tensor components.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the experimental observation of the SMD in $	ext{Co}_{1/3}	ext{TaS}_2$ (experiment), to developing a symmetry analysis and theoretical model incorporating SOC (theory), and finally confirming that the observed non-reciprocity is distinct from conventional magnetochiral effects (both).
why_interesting: The mechanism relies on intrinsic, spontaneous symmetry breaking driven by magnetic texture, which is a key concept in understanding topological and non-equilibrium quantum phenomena relevant to AMO physics.
